summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, Sjogren’s syndrome, POTS, and recent lupus diagnosis presented with hematemesis and recurrent nausea and vomiting. She had been started on prednisone for presumed lupus at a prior admission and was feeling well until two days before this admission. In the hospital, she had no active bleeding, stable hemoglobin, and an EGD showed no source of hemorrhage, with findings of a small hiatal hernia and duodenal atrophy. The bleeding was likely due to a Mallory-Weiss tear. Her abdominal pain was managed with medications, and she was transitioned to oral intake. Her prednisone was continued at a reduced dose, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her PCP regarding ongoing immunosuppressive therapy. A URI was treated by discontinuing Augmentin due to GI intolerance.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
